glosses: to betray

examples.text: Кто́-то вбил им в го́лову, что ка́ждое их поколе́ние обяза́тельно предаёт предыду́щее, и страх пре́дков стал у них подо́бием коллекти́вного невро́за.
examples.translation: Someone once hammered it into their heads that each generation inevitably betrays the one before it, and fear of their ancestors has assumed the proportions of a collective neurosis for them.
examples.english: Someone once hammered it into their heads that each generation inevitably betrays the one before it, and fear of their ancestors has assumed the proportions of a collective neurosis for them.

glosses: to expose, to subject, to commit, to hand over, to put
изменить, нарушить верность кому-либо, чему-либо

examples.text: Вот он здесь ещё живой и никого не предал и не продал ни на следствии, ни в лагере.

glosses: устар., книжн. выдать, отдать во власть, в распоряжение кого-либо

examples.text: — Ты нарочно под ногами путаешься? — зверея, закричал Иван, — я тебя самого предам в руки милиции!

glosses: подвергнуть какому-либо действию, привести в какое-либо состояние

examples.text: Если она скажет «да», отходы предадут огню, но на этом практика закончится.
Кто злословит отца своего или свою мать, того должно предать смерти.

glosses: To deliver into the hands of an enemy by treachery or fraud, in violation of trust; to give up treacherously or faithlessly.

examples.text: An officer betrayed the city.

glosses: To prove faithless or treacherous to, as to a trust or one who trusts; to be false to; to deceive.

examples.text: to betray a person or a cause
Quresh betrayed Sunil to marry Nuzhat.
My eyes have been betraying me since I turned sixty.

I maruell I heare no nevves of Dromio, either hee ſlackes the matter, or betraies his Maiſter, I dare not motion anie thing to Stellio, till I knovv vvhat my boy hath don, Ile hunt him out, if the loiterſacke be gone ſpringing into a Tauerne, Ile fetch him reeling out.

glosses: To violate the confidence of, by disclosing a secret, or that which one is bound in honor not to make known.
To disclose (a secret, etc.) in deliberate violation of someone’s confidence.

examples.text:
The dead leap at the throat, destroy
The meaning of the day; dark forms
Have scaled your walls, and spies betray
Old secrets to amorphous swarms.

glosses: To disclose or indicate, for example something which prudence would conceal; to reveal unintentionally.

examples.text: Though he had lived in England for many years, a faint accent betrayed his Swedish origin.

Jones’ sad eyes betray a pervasive pain his purposefully spare dialogue only hints at, while the perfectly cast [Josh] Brolin conveys hints of playfulness and warmth while staying true to the craggy stoicism at the character’s core.

Again, to take a less extreme example, there is no denying that although the dialects of northern France retained their fundamentally Romance character, they betray many Germanic influences in phonetics and vocabulary, […]

glosses: To mislead; to expose to inconvenience not foreseen; to lead into error or sin.
To lead astray; to seduce (as under promise of marriage) and then abandon.
Actuar en contra de alguien que confía en uno.
Ponerse en contra de una persona o institución que brinda apoyo.
No cumplir con lo que se promete o con un juramento hecho.
Transferir la propiedad de algo o prestar un servicio a cambio de un precio o pago.
Exhibir, presentar u ofrecer bienes o servicios a sus posibles compradores.
Presentar algo o hacer aparecer a alguien de una manera que atrae la aprobación de otros.
Faltar a la lealtad debida a algo o a alguien a cambio de un beneficio o interés material o personal.
Obtener un alto nivel de ventas o de aceptación pública.
Faire une perfidie à quelqu’un ; lui manquer de foi.

examples.text: Monsieur, répondit la reine, je puis ne pas aimer mon mari, mais personne n’a le droit d’exiger de moi que je le trahisse. De bonne foi, trahiriez-vous les secrets de la princesse de Porcian, votre femme ?
Je fus stupide et naïf, je méritai ce qui m'arriva. Je me fis détrousser. Peu m'importait l'argent que je perdis. On me trahit.

glosses: Manquer de respect ou de considération, en parlant des choses.

examples.text: Oui, mon père à peine en terre, j'étais coupable, oubliant mon deuil, trahissant mon chagrin et son souvenir.
Trahir les intérêts de quelqu’un, la confiance de son ami.
Trahir la vérité, sa conscience, son devoir, sa promesse, sa foi, ses serments.

glosses: Livrer son pays, sa patrie ; agir par perfidie contre la sécurité de son pays.
Découvrir ou révéler ce qu’on voulait tenir caché.

examples.text: Maudit accent qui me trahit toujours ! C’est vrai, j’arrive d’Italie.
Pensant à son accoutrement, il se défit de son faux-col et de sa casquette blanche d’aéronaute, qui pouvaient le trahir, […].
Sa figure intelligente, dont les traits et le teint trahissaient une assez forte proportion de sang soudanais, […], prenait par moments une expression de grande affabilité.
Rien dans son regard ne trahissait jamais la moindre pitié, c’était un pur soldat, dépourvu d’états d'âme.

glosses: Surprendre.

examples.text: S’il lui arrivait à présent de trahir un lapin au taillis, assis sur son derrière […].

glosses: Ne pas seconder, desservir, rendre vain, décevoir.

examples.text: La fortune a trahi nos efforts.
Les événements trahirent ses espérances.

glosses: Agir contre ses propres intérêts.

examples.text: Il s’est trahi lui-même en cette affaire.

glosses: The act of committing (e.g. a database transaction), making it a permanent change; such a change.

examples.text: To support locking and process synchronization independently of transaction commits, the server provides semaphore objects[…]
Every Git commit represents a single, atomic changeset with respect to the previous state.

glosses: The submission of source code or other material to a source control repository.
A person, especially a high school athlete, who agrees verbally or signs a letter committing to attend a college or university.
To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.

examples.text: Bid him farwell, commit him to the Graue,
Commit thy way vnto the Lord: trust also in him, and he shall bring it to passe.

If we take in hand any Volume; of Divinity or School Metaphyſics, for Inſtance; let us aſk, Does it contain any abſtract Reaſonings concerning Quantity or Number? No. Does it contain any experimental Reaſonings concerning Matters of Fact or Exiſtence? No. Commit it then to the Flames: For it can contain nothing but Sophiſtry and Illuſion.

glosses: To imprison: to forcibly place in a jail.

examples.text: and ſome of the Conſpirators committed to the Caſtle of Dublin by us

glosses: To forcibly evaluate and treat in a medical facility, particularly for presumed mental illness.

examples.text: Tony should be committed to a nuthouse!

glosses: To do (something bad); to perpetrate, as a crime, sin, or fault.

examples.text: to commit murder
to commit a series of heinous crimes
to commit suicide
Thou shalt not commit adultery.

glosses: To pledge or bind; to compromise, expose, or endanger by some decisive act or preliminary step. (Traditionally used only reflexively but now also without oneself etc.)

examples.text: to commit oneself to a certain action
to commit to a relationship

glosses: To physically place (something or someone somewhere).

examples.text: She put her books on the table.
The police put him in a cell.
They put the new motorway right through the national park.

Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm. Then he put the coffee pot on the stove and rummaged out a loaf of dry bread and some hardtack.
‘No. I only opened the door a foot and put my head in. The street lamps shine into that room. I could see him. He was all right. Sleeping like a great grampus. Poor, poor chap.’

glosses: To place in abstract; to attach or attribute; to assign.

examples.text: The government put restrictions on vehicle imports.
I put £100 on the winning horse.
Don't put the blame on me.
What answer did you put for question 3?
to put a wrong construction on an act or expression

glosses: To bring or set (into a certain relation, state or condition).

examples.text: Theſe Verſes Originally Greek, were put in Latin,
Put your house in order!

put to bed; put to shame; put to death; put into practice; put one's mind to it

glosses: To express (something in a certain manner).

examples.text: When you put it that way, I guess I can see your point.
To put it bluntly, he's an idiot.
All this is ingeniously and ably put.

glosses: To set before one for judgment, acceptance, or rejection; to bring to the attention.

examples.text: I put it to you, Sir, that you are a thief and a liar.
to put a question; to put a case

1708-1710, George Berkeley, Philosophical Commentaries or Common-Place Book
Put the perceptions and you put the mind.
Now if there was one thing that the animals were completely certain of, it was that they did not want Jones back. When it was put to them in this light, they had no more to say.

glosses: To set as a calculation or estimate.

examples.text: They have put the cost of repairs at around £10 million.

glosses: To steer; to direct one's course; to go.

examples.text: to put to sea
His fury thus appeased, he puts to land.

glosses: To sell (assets) under the terms of a put option.

examples.text: He got out of his Procter and Gamble bet by putting his shares at 80.

glosses: To throw with a pushing motion, especially in reference to the sport of shot put. (Do not confuse with putt.)

examples.text: He put the shot out beyond the 20-metre mark.

glosses: To play a card or a hand in the game called \"put\".
To lay down; to give up; to surrender.

examples.text: No man hath more love than this, that a man put his life for his friends.

glosses: To incite; to entice; to urge; to constrain; to oblige.

examples.text: These wretches put us upon all mischief.
Thank him who puts me loath to this revenge
Put me not to use the carnal weapon in my own defence.

glosses: To convey coal in the mine, as for example from the working to the tramway.
A right to sell something at a predetermined price.
Short for put option.

examples.text: He bought a January '08 put for Procter and Gamble at 80 to hedge his bet.

c. 1900, Universal Cyclopaedia Entry for Stock-Exchange
A put and a call may be combined in one instrument, the holder of which may either buy or sell as he chooses at the fixed price.

glosses: The act of putting; an action; a movement; a thrust; a push.

examples.text: the put of a ball
The Stag's was a Forc'd put, and a Chance rather than a Choice.

glosses: An old card game.

examples.text: Among the in-door amusements of the costermonger is card-playing, at which many of them are adepts. The usual games are all-fours, all-fives, cribbage, and put.

glosses: A fellow, especially an eccentric or elderly one; a duffer.

examples.text:
Queer Country-puts extol Queen Bess's reign,
And of lost hospitality complain.
The old put wanted to make a parson of me, but d—n me, thinks I to myself, I'll nick you there, old cull; the devil a smack of your nonsense shall you ever get into me.

Any number of varlet to be had for a few ducats and what droll puts the citizens seem in it all!
